articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Nov. 2: Notebook for Week 8

By Eric Moody

The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out to me.

Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills

Derrick Henry's playing time has declined over the past two weeks, falling below 50% of snaps against the Bills. On Sunday, he rushed for 53 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, marking his third straight game with fewer than 60 rushing yards. Justice Hill played on more snaps and ran more routes compared to Henry's nine, benefiting from Baltimore playing from behind. With Lamar Jackson headed for IR due to a thumb injury, the Ravens could struggle to sustain drives and generate red zone opportunities, making Henry's fantasy outlook even more concerning going forward.

Dalton Kincaid played through a chest injury against the Ravens and delivered his second-best fantasy performance (18.6 fantasy points) of the season, catching four out of six targets for 86 yards and a touchdown. Kincaid continues to share playing time with Dawson Knox, but his involvement in the passing game remains encouraging. He ran 23 routes (compared to Knox's 17) and his targets per route remain high despite a slight decline in snaps. Kincaid has now stockpiled 14 targets over his past two games and remains a solid TE1 heading into Week 9 against the Vikings.

Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals

Wan'Dale Robinson continues to be Tennessee's most reliable receiver. He led the Titans in both snaps and routes against the Bengals, catching six out of seven targets for 57 yards and a touchdown. He has now drawn at least six targets in four straight games and remains a flex option. Chimere Dike caught five passes for 71 yards and a touchdown while filling in for Carnell Tate, but his role could shrink after the Week 9 bye. TE Gunnar Helm had his best game of the season with five receptions for 76 yards on nine targets, despite playing on a season-low percentage of snaps. Daniel Bellinger's increased involvement makes Helm difficult to trust outside deeper leagues.

Chase Brown led Cincinnati's backfield in snaps, routes and touches against the Titans. Brown finished with 55 rushing yards on 12 carries and caught eight out of nine targets for 46 yards, scoring 16.1 fantasy points. He also ran more than twice as many routes as Samaje Perine, highlighting his significant role in the passing game. articles.descriptionJa: 標準的なリーグやより深いリーグにおいて、ロースターへの追加やストリーミングを検討すべき最優秀の獲得可能選手たち。
articles.body:
Each Monday, before the current NFL week ends, we will identify players worthy of your attention available in at least 50% of ESPN standard leagues. Things change quickly for player valuation and roles each week in the NFL, and free agency is a critical way to acquire players. We are here to help!

Top pick-up options at every position

Looking for the top recommendation at each skill position? Look no further! Here are the players to target heading into Week 9, along with their current roster percentages and a recommendation of how much of your free agent budget (FAB) to consider utilizing.

Geno Smith, QB, New York Jets (32.8% rostered, bid 3% of FAB)

Smith scored 18 points in the home loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, his third-best scoring output of the season. It was the third consecutive game Smith topped 250 passing yards, and only 14 passers have outscored him in fantasy this season. Smith is not a great play for Week 9 against the Kansas City Chiefs, but he has exciting receivers to throw to and certainly has been a useful fantasy option this season.

Note: The Tennessee Titans and Pittsburgh Steelers serve their bye weeks in Week 9. For those planning for Week 10, the Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles and Tampa Bay Buccaneers will not be playing.

Mike Washington Jr., RB, Las Vegas Raiders (17.6%, 3% FAB)

Washington was the beneficiary of a major -- albeit perhaps short-term -- alteration to the team's depth chart in Sunday's win over the Jets. Ashton Jeanty, the No. 6 pick in the 2025 draft, earned only five touches, though three of them were receptions that went for 64 yards. Jeanty scored 10.3 points. Washington rushed 25 times for 83 yards, scoring 8.3 points. The Raiders' split of touches may revert to prior to Week 8, as the New York Giants did recently with Cam Skattebo, but add Washington just in case it does not.

Jordyn Tyson, WR, New Orleans Saints (35.4%, 3% FAB)

The Saints did not play in Week 8, and rumors persist that Tyson (hamstring) will come off injured reserve to make his season debut in Week 9 against the Cleveland Browns. Tyson was the No. 8 pick in the 2026 NFL draft -- the second wide receiver selected after Carnell Tate -- and the Saints boast a quarterback averaging 39 pass attempts per game. This may be the final week Tyson will be readily available in your leagues.

Mike Gesicki, TE, Cincinnati Bengals (15.1%, 2% FAB)

Gesicki has caught a touchdown pass in five consecutive games, and six of seven this season. It's quite an achievement doing so despite low volume. No tight end has more touchdown catches, even though 26 tight ends have more receptions. Regardless, QB Joe Burrow looks for Gesicki in the red zone and the tight end matters for Week 9 against the Atlanta Falcons.

articles.headline: Jets' Aaron Glenn says he's not worried about job security amid tough start
articles.description: Jets coach Aaron Glenn insisted Monday that he's not concerned about his job security amid a three-game losing streak.
articles.headlineJa: ジェッツのアロン・グレン、不調なスタートの中でも解雇の不安はないと語る
articles.descriptionJa: ジェッツのアロン・グレンコーチは月曜日、3連敗という状況にあるが、自身の職の安定については懸念していないと強調した。
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- Aaron Glenn's seat is getting hotter by the week, but the New York Jets' coach insisted Monday that he's not concerned about his job security.

"There's so much that I think about when it comes to us improving each week that it really doesn't come across my mind, to be honest with you," Glenn told reporters on a video conference.

"I understand how this league is. I understand what this business is about, but my first job is each week improving this team. And that's the only thing that I think about."

The Jets have lost three in a row, falling to 2-6 -- only one game better than last season's eight-game record. Overall, Glenn is 5-20. The only team with a worse record in the same span is the Tennessee Titans (4-21).

Amid a rebuild, the Jets' organization didn't enter the season with playoff expectations. The plan was to evaluate Glenn based on progress.

Chairman Woody Johnson, who has endured 10 straight losing seasons, will make the ultimate call on Glenn's future. In 26 years of ownership, Johnson has made only one in-season coaching change -- Robert Saleh was fired only five games into the 2024 season.

Johnson, 79, hasn't spoken to the media in more than a year.

Glenn believes the team is heading in the right direction, but he knows the wins need to start coming soon.

"Absolutely," he said. "I mean, that's what this is. It's a bottom-line business, and we have to win, but we still have nine games left. So we still have an opportunity to win nine games."

The schedule gets tougher starting this week.

After losing back-to-back home games to the previously winless Miami Dolphins and the slumping Las Vegas Raiders, who had dropped four straight, the Jets travel to the Kansas City Chiefs (5-2), followed by a home date with the Buffalo Bills (6-1).

On Sunday, the Jets became only the third team in the past 45 years to lose a game after scoring on its first six possessions, per ESPN Research. Glenn, heavily criticized for in-game decisions and clock-management issues, made a few questionable moves Sunday. ESPN Analytics disagreed with three of his fourth-down decisions, noting there were two cases in which he reduced the team's win probability by kicking field goals instead of going for it.

Fans and media are calling for Glenn's job, but the players appear supportive.

"What I like about his leadership is he hasn't wavered, he hasn't flinched," said linebacker Demario Davis, a captain. "He's been the same guy every day. I believe in him. The guys believe in him."

Glenn received a five-year contract to return to the Jets, where he played and worked as a scout. The Jets started 0-7 last season and, despite talent upgrades in the offseason, the results haven't improved much.

The Jets have lost five games this season by a total of 25 points.

"It's incredibly frustrating," center Josh Myers said.

Tristan H. Cockcroft's 2026 fantasy football Knockout league rankings will be updated throughout the season to reflect the latest news, trends and opinions. Use them to inform your own rankings, or as a guide to draft your team. Sign up for your team for free.

Knockout leagues are our newest offering for 2026, challenging fantasy football managers to avoid being the last-place scorer in any given week, with the final team standing winning the championship. For those new to the format, here's a strategy primer to help you fine-tune your game.

The rankings below will differ slightly from our standard offering in that Knockout leagues begin with 18 teams, creating more demand at thinner positions such as quarterback and tight end. Additionally, week-over-week consistency carries additional weight, players with injury or other availability concerns are less desirable, and later-year bye weeks can prove advantageous. A standard 18-team knockout league comprises 14 slots including a kicker and a defense, so the rankings began 252 deep at season's start, and are now 140 deep (10 teams times 14 players) for leagues drafting to begin in Week 9, to take you from the first overall selection through to the final pick of the draft.

Remember that if you want to start a league that plays this week your draft must be completed by the time players lock for Thursday Night Football, otherwise your league will begin play the following week.  An 10-team league lets you eliminate nine players through Week 17, leaving only the winner standing.

The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. 

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders.

Hoop Collective: Is Houston an NBA Finals sleeper? And 76ers' dream start

Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to discuss the Houston Rockets' 6-1 start and whether they are a legitimate title contender. They then break down why Kyrie Irving might not be traded this season if the Dallas Mavericks' continue their impressive start to the season. Next, they check in on the injured Oklahoma City Thunder, the hot Memphis Grizzlies and the dream start for LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers.

Topics:

1:01: Houston impressing with 6-1 start to season

1:45: Windy Storytime: identifying contenders

4:35: Rockets looking the part of a contender

MacMahon on Kyrie's future in Dallas: "When I'm talking to executives and scouts around the league ... when the Mavericks come up, it is the No. 1 thing people are asking me about.

"You know, going into the season, I would have said more likely than not, [Irving] gets moved by the deadline, but I didn't feel super strong about it. The more I see the team, the more I'm around the team, the more I think it's going to be awfully hard to trade him.

"Not that there won't be a big market -- there will be, but if they've got a chance to compete for a play-in and playoff spot, I just think it's going to be really tough to move Kyrie. Also, just as much as he means to that locker room and as well as he's working with Cooper [Flagg], it was beautiful basketball.

"And just basketball wise they are a phenomenal fit. And I do think there's a legitimate argument to be made for the value of playing meaningful games in March and April for the development of a superstar like Cooper, of young role players like Zaccharie Risacher, who, by the way, is doing some really interesting things -- on the defensive end especially -- and he's got a player option next year.

"I think it's a situation where you can get together and handle it in the summer. It's not like you have to either move them or lose them, by this deadline."

articles.headline: Michael Carrick has 'no concerns' over Lisandro Martínez's commitment
articles.description: Michael Carrick has insisted he's got "no concerns" about Lisandro Martinez's commitment to Manchester United.
articles.headlineJa: マイケル・キャリック、リサンドロ・マルティネスの献身性に「懸念はない」
articles.descriptionJa: マイケル・キャリックは、リサンドロ・マルティネスのマンチェスター・ユナイテッドに対する献身性に「懸念はない」と強調した。
articles.body:
Michael Carrick has insisted he's got "no concerns" about Lisandro Martínez's commitment to Manchester United after the defender followed up his criticism of the club's board with a woeful performance against Chelsea.

Martínez was sent off at Stamford Bridge after giving away a penalty which allowed Chelsea to take a 2-0 lead.

In the last month, the Argentina international was also responsible for Tottenham's late equaliser in a 1-1 draw at Old Trafford and criticised director of football Jason Wilcox following the 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid.

The 28-year-old is out of contract at the end of the season and there have been suggestions that his behaviour -- on and off the pitch -- is linked to a desire to quit the club.

Carrick, however, has backed Martínez and insists the World Cup winner is determined to get back to his best.

"I've got no concerns about commitment at all," Carrick told a news conference on Tuesday.

"The dressing room is a good, good place. I've said it before, the commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other is I don't question that at all. We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but commitment's not a thing at all."

Carrick is under severe pressure following a run of nine games without a win.

- Ogden: Why Man United are so bad at hiring managers post-Ferguson

Club bosses are set to evaluate his position during the international break after games against Roma and Aston Villa this week. The 45-year-old's job is on the line, but he's choosing to remain positive ahead of two games which could decide his fate.

"I can look into the future, but you never know what's going to happen," Carrick said.

"That doesn't change how we're preparing for the game tomorrow, and I'm actually really looking forward to the game. I can't wait for the game tomorrow.

"You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had and what's going on, but I really can't wait for the game tomorrow, and that's all I'm focused on. Whatever happens is going to happen after that in whatever direction it goes in, but we want to make it a big night tomorrow night first."

United return to Old Trafford on Tuesday for the first time since the team was booed off after the dismal 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

While Carrick was applauded by supporters, the atmosphere changed once he disappeared down the tunnel and only the players were left on the pitch.

Kobbie Mainoo said he understands fans' frustration about how the season has started and admitted the squad need to give them something to shout about against Roma.

"In these tough times you can't expect the fans 100,000% of the time to be happy and cheering when we're not putting out results, you know," Mainoo said.

"We owe it to them to put the results out there for them to cheer again."

articles.headline: Noni Madueke: Alexis Mac Allister tried to 'bait me' into red card
articles.description: Noni Madueke has said that Alexis Mac Allister tried to "bait" him into getting a red card during Arsenal's 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield.
articles.headlineJa: ノニ・マドゥエケ：アレクシス・マク・アリスターにレッドカードを狙って「挑発された」
articles.descriptionJa: ノニ・マドゥエケは、アンフィールドで行われたリヴァプール対アーセナルの試合（アーセナルが1-0で勝利）において、アレクシス・マク・アリスターがレッドカードを誘うために自分を「挑発」しようとしたと語った。
articles.body:
Noni Madueke has said that Alexis Mac Allister tried to "bait" him into getting a red card during Arsenal's 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield.

The Argentine midfielder went to ground while he and Madueke were face-to-face in the 79th minute of the match and Madueke was not punished.

Speaking to reporters after the match, Madueke said that he didn't think there was "anything" in the incident.

"To be honest, I don't think it's anything -- a yellow card or a red card. The referee didn't think that, VAR [Video Assistant Referee] didn't think that, so we all agreed there," the Arsenal forward said.

"It's a natural movement and he's obviously clever, he tried to bait me into getting a red card there but obviously no. In my head, I was thinking it's possible [to be sent off] with VAR, with whoever interprets it -- I don't know what they're thinking... But thankfully it wasn't."

The Gunners claimed victory at Anfield for the first time in 14 years as Kai Havertz scored the only goal of the game.

Mac Allister was criticised by Jamie Carragher for his role in the incident between himself and Madueke

On Sky Sports, Carragher said: "I am delighted [Madueke] never got sent off there. "We have got to be strong in calling people out and saying 'this is embarrassing.'

"It has got to stop, it's ridiculous. I can't stand it.

"If someone puts their head back then butts, of course it's a red card. But this stuff about a head-to-head, and if someone touches the other one goes down and it's a red card?

- Arsenal hold on for a big win at Liverpool, one Iraola & Co. can learn from

- Declan Rice tops Premier League assist chart - without set-pieces

- Dominik Szoboszlai asks if Liverpool expected to 'dive' to win penalty

"As a game, as football, people in the Premier League and supporters [must] call your own people out for it.

"I am a Liverpool fan and that's a joke from Mac Allister. It's got to stop.

"People are trying to game the system because they know that they can. Red cards are being given for it.

"Whether it's from Howard Webb, the Premier League, the managers -- stop getting red cards for this."

articles.headline: Xabi Alonso: Romeo Lavia 'in top form' after Chelsea beat Man United
articles.description: Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso believes the club is finally seeing the best of Romeo Lavia, with the midfielder "in a good place" after putting his injury problems behind him.
articles.body:
Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso believes the club is finally seeing the best of Romeo Lavia, with the midfielder "in a good place" after putting his injury problems behind him.

The 22-year-old has faced a lengthy fitness struggle since signing from Southampton in 2023 and had not completed a competitive 90 minutes for the Blues until last week's Carabao Cup tie against Liverpool.

But he followed that up by going the distance for the second time in four days, turning in a fine display in a 2-0 win over Manchester United.

"We know Rom is feeling better, is feeling stronger, is feeling more confident to go with more minutes and with more load," Alonso told the club's official website.

"He's gone from playing the whole game at Anfield to not even 72 hours later playing that way and with that energy [against United]. Sometimes the head is more important than the legs and now his head is in a good place."

Alonso knows the mechanics of controlling the midfield better than most, having pulled the strings at the highest level with Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain, and was full of praise for Lavia's work against the Red Devils.

"It was a top performance. In the last three weeks, I've seen Romeo in top form," he said.

- Premier League VAR review: Liverpool denied a penalty vs. Arsenal?

- Man United implode at Chelsea; they are now in Premier League relegation battle

- Michael Carrick on the brink as Man United lose at Chelsea

"His game, from a midfielder's point of view, was very complete. He has done so many good things and I'm happy for him. He deserves huge recognition.

"He has done so many things right. He was always connecting the defence with the attacking players, he was able to switch the game, he has taken many right decisions, was very dynamic and competitive.

"Not just this game but in the last two or three weeks, he has been playing at a very good level and I'm very happy for him."

articles.headline: Barcelona's Anthony Gordon ahead of Aston Villa: 'I can do a lot more'
articles.description: Anthony Gordon said Barcelona have not seen the best of him yet as he promises to become more selfish ahead of Tuesday's Champions League game vs. Aston Villa.
articles.body:
BARCELONA -- Anthony Gordon said Barcelona have not seen the best of him yet as he promises to become more selfish ahead of Tuesday's Champions League game against Aston Villa at Spotify Camp Nou.

Gordon, a €70 million summer signing from Newcastle United, has made an encouraging start to life at Barça, scoring three goals and providing five assists so far.

The England international's most recent goal came in Saturday's 6-1 victory over Alavés, a lovely dinked finish over the goalkeeper, but he says there is more to come as he prepares to face Premier League opposition for the first time since moving to Spain.

"I have started quite well considering it's a new country for me, maybe 7.5 out of 10," he said in a news conference on Monday.

"It's a massive change. It's a new team, although the new country is the biggest part. I have started well, but I can do a lot more.

"It will take some time for me to really settle and grow. When this happens, you will see the very best of me, which you definitely haven't seen so far."

To reach the next level, Gordon says he is aware he must be more selfish at times.

"My demands are always the same, to score, to assist, to be someone who can change a game in any moment and to take responsibility for the game," he said.

"The best in history do this, so that is what I chase. I think I can do it more, be more selfish sometimes, dribble and shoot more. This is the big focus -- definitely to score more goals.

"The challenge here at Barça is different to what I had before. At Everton, I was fighting relegation, which was tough; Newcastle's [objective] was [to quality for the] Champions League or to push up the table.

"Now it's trophies, so three very different challenges. I have really enjoyed all three. To be competing on every front, for every trophy, is definitely the most enjoyable.

"People think that is more pressure, but it's better pressure than fighting relegation or trying to climb the table."

During a recent international break, Gordon suggested he has gained a newfound respect back in his native England after moving to Barcelona in the summer. 

However, he wanted to clarify that he did not mean people had a negative opinion of in his homeland, just that Barça's style of play gives him the chance to showcase other attributes.

"When I said that, I didn't mean people were judging me wrong," he said.

"I meant they had never seen me in a system that highlights these qualities. Like I said before, I have played in three different styles of team; that probably shows the intelligence I am talking about to be able to succeed in all three.

"I wasn't saying people judge me wrong or have a negative perspective of me, just that they hadn't seen me in this kind of system before, which I think now is helping them appreciate me a little bit more."

articles.headline: Arsenal got a big win at Liverpool, but why no Isak penalty?
articles.description: Arsenal got a big win at Liverpool to go clear atop the Premier League, but Liverpool should have had a penalty. Plus: Michael Carrick's Man United future, Milan's bounce-back, Bayern's frustrations and more.
articles.body:
What a weekend in soccer! Europe's top leagues delivered, as they always do, when it comes to talking points.

In the Premier League's big games, Arsenal got a huge win (and a little luck) Sunday in breaking a historic winless streak at Liverpool dating back to 2012, while Man United sank from bad to worse in losing heavily at Chelsea on Saturday.

In LaLiga, Real Madrid got a win that should make Jose Mourinho happy for how they did it (scoring early and often), while Bayern Munich drew against Borussia Dortmund in Der Klassiker, a game they really, really should have won. In Serie A, Ruben Amorim (remember him, Man United fans?) and Milan won the derby over Inter to cap a tough week in the best possible way. We also got narratives galore from Brighton (how do they keep doing it?), Tottenham (yes, they're back), Juventus (shoutout to Kerim Alajbegovic), Barcelona (who rebounded from the Clasico loss in fine fashion) and much more.

It's Monday morning, so what better time for some musings? Let's get into it.

- United implode at Chelsea; they are now in Premier League relegation battle

- Arsenal hold on for a big win at Liverpool, one Iraola & Co. can learn from

- What soccer stars did for Halloween: James the Joker, DracuLucas, more

Arsenal get big win at Liverpool, but referees owe us answers

I'll get this out of the way and get to what we really want to talk about which is, you know, football.

Liverpool should have had a penalty for Jurriën Timber's shirt-pull on Alexander Isak -- there's really no gray area. If referee Andy Madley didn't see it clearly or deemed it (as some have suggested) "normal physical jockeying," VAR Stuart Attwell should have sent him to the monitor to have another look. There's nothing normal about grabbing an opponent's shirt, and it doesn't take a physicist to figure out that without the tug, Isak would have headed the ball goalward.

In fact, it could have been a denial of goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO) situation. Law 12 is pretty clear: "Where a player ... denies an obvious goal-scoring opportunity and the referee awards a penalty kick, the offender is cautioned if the offence was an attempt to play the ball or a challenge for the ball: in all other circumstances [holding, pulling, pushing, etc.] the offending player must be sent off."

This is as open and shut as you're going to see. And please, don't spread the nonsense theory that Isak "should have made more of the pull" to influence the ref. I don't want to see players trying to "win" penalties, and certainly not when it's that obvious. I just want the VAR to help the referee do his job. (And I'm pretty sure Andoni Iraola feels the same way despite what he said postgame.)

Heck, later in the same game we had a perfect example of a player "making the most of it" to try to influence the referee. Alexis Mac Allister throwing himself to the ground, and staying there, writhing in pain, after being brushed by Noni Madueke's forehead was simply embarrassing. I
